topic: Medicaid and Coverage Options for Pregnant Virginians 2026

title.en: Pregnant in Virginia? Medicaid + Coverage Options 2026
title.es: ¿Embarazada en Virginia? Medicaid + Opciones de Cobertura 2026

description.en: Pregnant in Virginia 2026? Cardinal Care Medicaid covers to 148% FPL, FAMIS MOMS to 205% FPL, and a new pregnancy SEP opens Virginia's Marketplace anytime.
description.es: ¿Embarazada en Virginia en 2026? Cardinal Care cubre hasta 148% FPL, FAMIS MOMS hasta 205% FPL, y un nuevo SEP abre el Mercado de Virginia en cualquier momento.

h1.en: Pregnant in Virginia in 2026? Here Are Your Health Coverage Options
h1.es: ¿Embarazada en Virginia en 2026? Aqui Estan Sus Opciones de Cobertura

subhero.en: Virginia Cardinal Care (Medicaid) covers prenatal care up to 148% FPL with no waiting period. FAMIS MOMS extends coverage to 205% FPL. A new Virginia law effective January 31, 2026 lets you enroll in the state Marketplace anytime during pregnancy with a 60-day window once you start the process.
subhero.es: Virginia Cardinal Care (Medicaid) cubre atencion prenatal hasta 148% FPL sin periodo de espera. FAMIS MOMS extiende la cobertura al 205% FPL. Una nueva ley de Virginia efectiva el 31 de enero de 2026 le permite inscribirse en el Mercado estatal en cualquier momento durante el embarazo, con una ventana de 60 dias una vez que inicia el proceso.

heading.en: You can enroll in Virginia Medicaid or FAMIS MOMS year-round during pregnancy
heading.es: Puede inscribirse en Medicaid de Virginia o FAMIS MOMS todo el ano durante el embarazo

body.en: Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS accept applications year-round with no enrollment deadline during pregnancy. Presumptive eligibility allows prenatal care to begin immediately at a qualified provider while your full application is processed. For the new Virginia Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP (effective January 31, 2026), you must start the enrollment process while still pregnant and then complete enrollment within 60 days of starting. Postpartum coverage continues for 12 full months after delivery regardless of income changes.
body.es: Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid y FAMIS MOMS aceptan solicitudes todo el ano sin fecha limite durante el embarazo. La elegibilidad presuntiva permite comenzar la atencion prenatal de inmediato con un proveedor calificado mientras se procesa su solicitud completa. Para el nuevo SEP de embarazo del Mercado de Seguros de Virginia (efectivo 31 de enero de 2026), debe iniciar el proceso de inscripcion mientras aun este embarazada y completar la inscripcion en 60 dias. La cobertura postparto continua por 12 meses completos despues del parto independientemente de los cambios de ingreso.

label.en: Virginia Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP (once started: 60 days to complete)
label.es: SEP de embarazo del Mercado de Virginia (una vez iniciado: 60 dias para completar)

label.en: Postpartum Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS (12 months after delivery)
label.es: Medicaid postparto y FAMIS MOMS (12 meses despues del parto)

quickAnswer.en: Pregnant Virginians in 2026 have three main coverage paths: (1) Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid (free, year-round, up to 148% FPL, which equals about $32,028 for a 2-person household since the expected baby counts), (2) FAMIS MOMS (Virginia CHIP for pregnant women, up to 205% FPL, about $44,362 for a 2-person household), or (3) Virginia Insurance Marketplace private plan using the new pregnancy-specific Special Enrollment Period available anytime during pregnancy. All three paths cover prenatal care, labor and delivery, and 12 months of postpartum coverage. Apply through CommonHelp at commonhelp.virginia.gov or Virginia's Insurance Marketplace at marketplace.virginia.gov.
quickAnswer.es: Las virginianas embarazadas en 2026 tienen tres rutas principales de cobertura: (1) Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid (gratis, todo el ano, hasta 148% FPL, lo que equivale a unos $32,028 para un hogar de 2 personas ya que el bebe esperado cuenta), (2) FAMIS MOMS (CHIP de Virginia para mujeres embarazadas, hasta 205% FPL, unos $44,362 para un hogar de 2 personas), o (3) plan privado del Mercado de Seguros de Virginia usando el nuevo Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de embarazo disponible en cualquier momento durante el embarazo. Las tres rutas cubren atencion prenatal, parto y 12 meses de cobertura postparto.

introParagraphs.en: Pregnancy in Virginia triggers immediate access to health coverage options that are available year-round, unlike most other life events that impose strict 60-day deadlines. Virginia Cardinal Care is the state's Medicaid program administered by the Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services (DMAS). Cardinal Care for pregnant women covers prenatal visits, labor and delivery, postpartum care, and prescription drugs at no cost for Virginians whose household income falls at or below 148% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level. A pregnant woman counts as two people when calculating household size for this program, so the actual income threshold for a pregnant woman with no other dependents is $32,028 per year (148% FPL at household size 2 under 2026 guidelines). Presumptive eligibility through Cardinal Care means that a qualified provider such as an OB-GYN or certified nurse-midwife can enroll you on the spot for immediate prenatal coverage while your formal Medicaid application is reviewed. Apply online at commonhelp.virginia.gov, through the CoverVA portal at coverva.dmas.virginia.gov, or by calling Virginia DMAS at 1-855-242-8282.
introParagraphs.es: El embarazo en Virginia activa el acceso inmediato a opciones de cobertura de salud disponibles todo el ano, a diferencia de la mayoria de otros eventos de vida que imponen plazos estrictos de 60 dias. Virginia Cardinal Care es el programa Medicaid del estado administrado por el Departamento de Servicios de Asistencia Medica (DMAS) de Virginia. Cardinal Care para mujeres embarazadas cubre visitas prenatales, parto, atencion postparto y medicamentos recetados sin costo para las virginianas cuyo ingreso familiar sea igual o inferior al 148% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026. Una mujer embarazada cuenta como dos personas al calcular el tamano del hogar para este programa, por lo que el umbral de ingreso real para una mujer embarazada sin otros dependientes es de $32,028 por ano (148% FPL en tamano de hogar 2 segun las pautas de 2026). La elegibilidad presuntiva a traves de Cardinal Care significa que un proveedor calificado puede inscribirla al instante para cobertura prenatal inmediata mientras se revisa su solicitud formal de Medicaid.

introParagraphs.en: FAMIS MOMS is Virginia's separate CHIP program for pregnant women whose income exceeds the Medicaid limit. FAMIS MOMS covers income up to 205% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level, which equals $44,362 per year for a 2-person household (pregnant woman plus expected child) or $56,006 for a 3-person household. FAMIS MOMS coverage includes the same prenatal, delivery, and postpartum benefits as Cardinal Care but with a small premium or cost-sharing for higher-income enrollees. A third option became available effective January 31, 2026: a new pregnancy-specific Special Enrollment Period for Virginia's state-based Insurance Marketplace. This SEP allows any qualifying pregnant Virginian who is not already enrolled in Marketplace coverage to enroll in a private plan at any point during pregnancy. The Marketplace SEP requires the enrollee to initiate enrollment within the pregnancy and then complete it within 60 days of starting. Premium Tax Credits are available for Marketplace plans if household income falls between 100% and 400% of FPL. All three programs, which are Cardinal Care Medicaid, FAMIS MOMS, and the Marketplace pregnancy SEP, extend postpartum coverage for 12 months after delivery regardless of income changes. Babies born to Medicaid-enrolled mothers are automatically enrolled in Medicaid at birth under the deemed newborn rule.
introParagraphs.es: FAMIS MOMS es el programa CHIP separado de Virginia para mujeres embarazadas cuyo ingreso supera el limite de Medicaid. FAMIS MOMS cubre hasta el 205% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026, que equivale a $44,362 por ano para un hogar de 2 personas o $56,006 para un hogar de 3 personas. FAMIS MOMS incluye los mismos beneficios prenatales, de parto y postparto que Cardinal Care pero con una pequena prima o participacion en costos para inscriptas de mayores ingresos. Una tercera opcion estuvo disponible a partir del 31 de enero de 2026: un nuevo Periodo de Inscripcion Especial especifico para el embarazo para el Mercado de Seguros estatal de Virginia. Este SEP permite a cualquier virginianas embarazada calificada que no este inscrita en el Mercado inscribirse en un plan privado en cualquier momento durante el embarazo. Los tres programas extienden la cobertura postparto por 12 meses despues del parto independientemente de los cambios de ingreso.

name.en: Calculate your household size and projected 2026 income
name.es: Calcule el tamano de su hogar y el ingreso proyectado para 2026

text.en: Count the expected baby as a household member from the day you apply, since Virginia uses this approach when determining Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS eligibility for pregnant women. Use your projected annual income for the rest of 2026, not your prior-year tax return. Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) is the income standard for all Virginia pregnancy Medicaid programs and includes wages, self-employment income, and unemployment compensation.
text.es: Cuente al bebe esperado como miembro del hogar desde el dia que solicita, ya que Virginia usa este enfoque al determinar la elegibilidad de Medicaid y FAMIS MOMS para mujeres embarazadas. Use su ingreso anual proyectado para el resto de 2026, no su declaracion de impuestos del ano anterior. El Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) es el estandar de ingresos para todos los programas de Medicaid de embarazo de Virginia.

name.en: Check whether you qualify for Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid (free coverage, 148% FPL)
name.es: Verifique si califica para Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid (cobertura gratuita, 148% FPL)

text.en: Cardinal Care Medicaid for pregnant women covers income up to 148% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level. For a 2-person household (you plus expected baby), the 2026 income limit is $32,028 per year. For a 3-person household, the limit is $40,434. If your income qualifies, apply immediately at commonhelp.virginia.gov or coverva.dmas.virginia.gov. Cardinal Care is free with no monthly premiums and covers all prenatal care, delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care.
text.es: Cardinal Care Medicaid para mujeres embarazadas cubre ingresos hasta el 148% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026. Para un hogar de 2 personas (usted mas el bebe esperado), el limite de ingreso 2026 es $32,028 por ano. Para un hogar de 3 personas, el limite es $40,434. Si su ingreso califica, solicite de inmediato en commonhelp.virginia.gov o coverva.dmas.virginia.gov. Cardinal Care es gratuito sin primas mensuales y cubre toda la atencion prenatal, el parto y 12 meses de atencion postparto.

name.en: If income is above 148% FPL, apply for FAMIS MOMS (coverage up to 205% FPL)
name.es: Si el ingreso supera 148% FPL, solicite FAMIS MOMS (cobertura hasta 205% FPL)

text.en: FAMIS MOMS is Virginia's CHIP program for pregnant women who earn too much for Cardinal Care but too little for a Marketplace plan without significant subsidies. The 2026 income limit is 205% FPL: $44,362 for a 2-person household, $56,006 for a 3-person household. FAMIS MOMS is administered through the same CoverVA portal and includes comprehensive prenatal and postpartum benefits. Apply at coverva.dmas.virginia.gov or by calling 1-855-242-8282.
text.es: FAMIS MOMS es el programa CHIP de Virginia para mujeres embarazadas que ganan demasiado para Cardinal Care pero no lo suficiente para un plan del Mercado sin subsidios significativos. El limite de ingreso 2026 es 205% FPL: $44,362 para un hogar de 2 personas, $56,006 para un hogar de 3 personas. FAMIS MOMS se administra a traves del mismo portal CoverVA e incluye beneficios prenatales y postparto completos. Solicite en coverva.dmas.virginia.gov o llamando al 1-855-242-8282.

name.en: If income exceeds 205% FPL, use the Virginia Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP
name.es: Si el ingreso supera 205% FPL, use el SEP de embarazo del Mercado de Seguros de Virginia

text.en: Effective January 31, 2026, Virginia created a pregnancy-specific Special Enrollment Period for its state-based Insurance Marketplace. This SEP lets qualifying pregnant Virginians who are not already enrolled in Marketplace coverage sign up for a private plan at any point during pregnancy. Once you start the enrollment process, you have 60 days to complete it. Visit marketplace.virginia.gov to compare Silver, Gold, and Bronze plans. Premium Tax Credits reduce monthly costs if household income falls between 100% and 400% FPL (the ACA subsidy cliff returned for 2026 after enhanced PTCs expired January 1, 2026). At tax time, Virginia Marketplace enrollees who received Premium Tax Credits will use Form 1095-A to reconcile actual credits against estimated credits on their federal tax return.
text.es: Desde el 31 de enero de 2026, Virginia creo un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial especifico para el embarazo para su Mercado de Seguros estatal. Este SEP permite a las virginianas embarazadas calificadas que no esten inscritas en el Mercado inscribirse en un plan privado en cualquier momento durante el embarazo. Una vez que inicia el proceso, tiene 60 dias para completarlo. Visite marketplace.virginia.gov para comparar planes Silver, Gold y Bronze. Los Creditos Fiscales de Prima reducen los costos mensuales si el ingreso familiar cae entre 100% y 400% FPL.

name.en: Request presumptive eligibility for immediate prenatal care
name.es: Solicite elegibilidad presuntiva para atencion prenatal inmediata

text.en: Virginia Cardinal Care offers presumptive eligibility for pregnant women: your OB-GYN, midwife, or prenatal clinic can determine your likely eligibility on the spot and authorize Medicaid coverage immediately for prenatal care while your full application is reviewed. Ask your healthcare provider whether they are a qualified entity for Virginia presumptive eligibility determinations. Coverage begins the same day the provider makes the determination, so you can start your prenatal visits without waiting for formal approval.
text.es: Virginia Cardinal Care ofrece elegibilidad presuntiva para mujeres embarazadas: su ginecologo-obstetra, partera o clinica prenatal puede determinar su probable elegibilidad en el momento y autorizar cobertura de Medicaid de inmediato para atencion prenatal mientras se revisa su solicitud completa. Pregunte a su proveedor de salud si es una entidad calificada para determinaciones de elegibilidad presuntiva de Virginia.

name.en: Confirm your baby's automatic Medicaid enrollment at birth
name.es: Confirme la inscripcion automatica de Medicaid de su bebe al nacer

text.en: Babies born to a Cardinal Care Medicaid-enrolled mother are automatically enrolled in Virginia Medicaid at birth under the deemed newborn rule, with coverage retroactive to the date of birth. The hospital submits the newborn enrollment on your behalf. If your income at delivery is higher than the Medicaid limit, your newborn may qualify for FAMIS (Virginia CHIP for children up to 205% FPL) or Cardinal Care for children. Notify your DMAS case worker or call 1-855-242-8282 if your baby is not enrolled within 2 to 3 weeks of birth.
text.es: Los bebes nacidos de una madre inscrita en Cardinal Care Medicaid se inscriben automaticamente en Medicaid de Virginia al nacer bajo la regla del recien nacido calificado, con cobertura retroactiva a la fecha de nacimiento. El hospital envia la inscripcion del recien nacido en su nombre. Si su ingreso al momento del parto es superior al limite de Medicaid, su bebe puede calificar para FAMIS (CHIP de Virginia para ninos hasta 205% FPL).

name.en: Maintain 12-month postpartum coverage regardless of income changes
name.es: Mantenga 12 meses de cobertura postparto independientemente de los cambios de ingreso

text.en: Virginia extends Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS coverage for 12 full months after the end of pregnancy, per the American Rescue Plan Act postpartum extension now permanent in Virginia. During this postpartum year, coverage cannot be terminated due to income increases above 148% or 205% FPL. If you return to work and your income rises significantly, contact your DMAS case worker at 1-855-242-8282 to understand your transition options after the 12-month postpartum period ends. At that point, you may qualify for standard Virginia Medicaid expansion coverage (138% FPL) or a Marketplace plan with a qualifying life event SEP.
text.es: Virginia extiende la cobertura de Medicaid y FAMIS MOMS por 12 meses completos despues del fin del embarazo, segun la extension postparto de la Ley del Plan de Rescate Americano ahora permanente en Virginia. Durante este ano postparto, la cobertura no puede terminarse debido a aumentos de ingresos por encima del 148% o 205% FPL. Si regresa al trabajo y sus ingresos aumentan significativamente, contacte a su trabajador de caso de DMAS al 1-855-242-8282 para entender sus opciones de transicion.

footnote.en: Virginia expanded Medicaid in 2019 and currently covers adults at up to 138% FPL through Cardinal Care. Pregnancy Medicaid uses higher thresholds (148% for Cardinal Care, 205% for FAMIS MOMS). All programs extend postpartum coverage for 12 months after delivery. The 2026 ACA subsidy cliff at 400% FPL returned after enhanced premium tax credits expired January 1, 2026.
footnote.es: Virginia expandio Medicaid en 2019 y actualmente cubre a adultos hasta 138% FPL a traves de Cardinal Care. Medicaid de embarazo usa umbrales mas altos (148% para Cardinal Care, 205% para FAMIS MOMS). Todos los programas extienden la cobertura postparto por 12 meses despues del parto. El precipicio de subsidio ACA 2026 al 400% FPL regreso despues de que los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados vencieron el 1 de enero de 2026.

intro.en: The most costly mistakes pregnant Virginians make when navigating coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que cometen las virginianas embarazadas al buscar cobertura en 2026:

items.en: Not counting the expected baby in household size. Virginia Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS count the expected baby as a household member, making the income threshold higher than most people expect. A pregnant woman alone is a 2-person household for these programs.
items.es: No contar al bebe esperado en el tamano del hogar. Medicaid de Virginia y FAMIS MOMS cuentan al bebe esperado como miembro del hogar, lo que hace el umbral de ingreso mas alto de lo que la mayoria espera. Una mujer embarazada sola es un hogar de 2 personas para estos programas.

items.en: Waiting too long to apply. Virginia offers presumptive eligibility for prenatal care, so coverage can begin the same day a qualified healthcare provider screens you. Delaying application means paying out-of-pocket for early prenatal visits that should be free.
items.es: Esperar demasiado para solicitar. Virginia ofrece elegibilidad presuntiva para atencion prenatal, por lo que la cobertura puede comenzar el mismo dia que un proveedor calificado la evalua. Retrasar la solicitud significa pagar de su bolsillo visitas prenatales tempranas que deberian ser gratuitas.

items.en: Assuming the federal healthcare.gov Marketplace is where to enroll. Virginia operates its own state-based Insurance Marketplace at marketplace.virginia.gov. The 2026 pregnancy SEP is a Virginia-specific benefit not available in all states.
items.es: Asumir que el Mercado federal healthcare.gov es donde inscribirse. Virginia opera su propio Mercado de Seguros estatal en marketplace.virginia.gov. El SEP de embarazo de 2026 es un beneficio especifico de Virginia no disponible en todos los estados.

items.en: Enrolling in COBRA without checking Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS first. COBRA continuation charges 102% of the full employer premium, often $500 to $2,000 per month. Cardinal Care Medicaid covers the same prenatal care at zero cost if income qualifies, and FAMIS MOMS keeps costs very low.
items.es: Inscribirse en COBRA sin verificar primero Medicaid y FAMIS MOMS. La continuacion COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima completa del empleador, a menudo $500 a $2,000 al mes. Cardinal Care Medicaid cubre la misma atencion prenatal sin costo si el ingreso califica, y FAMIS MOMS mantiene los costos muy bajos.

items.en: Not knowing about the 12-month postpartum coverage guarantee. Virginia Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS coverage continues for exactly 12 months after the end of pregnancy regardless of income changes. Some enrollees wrongly believe coverage ends at delivery or 60 days postpartum.
items.es: No saber sobre la garantia de cobertura postparto de 12 meses. La cobertura de Medicaid y FAMIS MOMS de Virginia continua por exactamente 12 meses despues del fin del embarazo independientemente de los cambios de ingreso. Algunas inscriptas creen erroneamente que la cobertura termina al parto o a los 60 dias postparto.

items.en: Missing the baby's Medicaid enrollment window if the mother is not on Medicaid at delivery. Newborns born to Medicaid-enrolled mothers are auto-enrolled. But if the mother transitions to a Marketplace plan before delivery, the newborn triggers a 60-day SEP and must be enrolled separately within that window.
items.es: Perder la ventana de inscripcion de Medicaid del bebe si la madre no esta en Medicaid al momento del parto. Los recien nacidos de madres inscritas en Medicaid se inscriben automaticamente. Pero si la madre pasa a un plan del Mercado antes del parto, el recien nacido activa un SEP de 60 dias y debe inscribirse por separado dentro de esa ventana.

heading.en: Virginia's New Pregnancy SEP for the Insurance Marketplace (Effective January 31, 2026)
heading.es: Nuevo SEP de Embarazo de Virginia para el Mercado de Seguros (Efectivo 31 de Enero de 2026)

paragraphs.en: Virginia's Insurance Marketplace at marketplace.virginia.gov is a state-run exchange separate from the federal healthcare.gov that most other states use. Virginia debuted its own state-based Marketplace in the fall of 2023, and all Virginia residents shop for private ACA plans through marketplace.virginia.gov, not healthcare.gov. Effective January 31, 2026, a new state law led by Delegate Irene Shin created a pregnancy-specific Special Enrollment Period for Virginia's Marketplace. Before this law, becoming pregnant was not a qualifying life event under federal ACA rules, meaning that a pregnant Virginian who missed Open Enrollment and did not have another qualifying life event (such as job loss or marriage) could be locked out of Marketplace coverage for the entire year. The new Virginia pregnancy SEP changes this by allowing any qualifying pregnant person who is not already enrolled in a Marketplace plan to start enrollment at any point during the pregnancy. Once enrollment is started, the applicant has 60 days to complete it and select a plan. The SEP is not available to individuals who are already enrolled in a Marketplace plan (they cannot use it to switch plans mid-year). Maternity care and childbirth are essential health benefits covered by all Virginia Marketplace plans, and coverage applies even if pregnancy began before the enrollment date. Premium Tax Credits are available to reduce monthly premiums for households with income between 100% and 400% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level. The 400% FPL subsidy cliff returned for 2026 after the enhanced premium tax credits from the Inflation Reduction Act expired on January 1, 2026.
paragraphs.es: El Mercado de Seguros de Virginia en marketplace.virginia.gov es un intercambio estatal separado del federal healthcare.gov que usan la mayoria de los demas estados. Virginia inauguro su propio Mercado estatal en otono de 2023, y todos los residentes de Virginia compran planes privados ACA a traves de marketplace.virginia.gov. A partir del 31 de enero de 2026, una nueva ley estatal creo un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial especifico para el embarazo para el Mercado de Virginia. Antes de esta ley, quedar embarazada no era un evento calificador de vida bajo las reglas federales de la ACA. El nuevo SEP de embarazo de Virginia cambia esto al permitir que cualquier persona embarazada calificada que no este inscrita en un plan del Mercado comience la inscripcion en cualquier momento durante el embarazo. Una vez iniciada la inscripcion, la solicitante tiene 60 dias para completarla. Los Creditos Fiscales de Prima estan disponibles para reducir las primas mensuales para hogares con ingresos entre 100% y 400% del FPL 2026.

heading.en: What Documents Pregnant Virginians Need to Apply for Coverage in 2026
heading.es: Que Documentos Necesitan las Virginianas Embarazadas para Solicitar Cobertura en 2026

paragraphs.en: Cardinal Care Medicaid and FAMIS MOMS applications require standard identity, residency, income, and pregnancy verification documents. Gathering these before starting the online application at commonhelp.virginia.gov significantly reduces processing delays. Most applications are processed within 45 days, but presumptive eligibility provides coverage immediately if a qualified provider determines likely eligibility during a prenatal visit. For the Virginia Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP at marketplace.virginia.gov, documentation requirements are similar to standard ACA enrollment but include pregnancy verification to trigger the SEP. Virginia DMAS and the Marketplace both accept digital copies of documents uploaded through the online portal.
paragraphs.es: Las solicitudes de Cardinal Care Medicaid y FAMIS MOMS requieren documentos estandar de identidad, residencia, ingresos y verificacion de embarazo. Reunirlos antes de iniciar la solicitud en linea en commonhelp.virginia.gov reduce significativamente los retrasos en el procesamiento. La mayoria de las solicitudes se procesan en 45 dias, pero la elegibilidad presuntiva proporciona cobertura de inmediato si un proveedor calificado determina la probable elegibilidad durante una visita prenatal.

heading.en: Cardinal Care vs FAMIS MOMS vs Marketplace: Which Virginia Coverage Should You Choose?
heading.es: Cardinal Care vs FAMIS MOMS vs Mercado: Que Cobertura de Virginia Debe Elegir?

paragraphs.en: Three programs serve pregnant Virginians in 2026 and the decision flows logically from income. Cardinal Care Medicaid is the first check: if household income (counting the expected baby) falls at or below 148% FPL ($32,028 for a 2-person household in 2026), Cardinal Care is free, covers everything, and should be the automatic choice. FAMIS MOMS is the bridge program for income between 148% and 205% FPL ($32,028 to $44,362 for a 2-person household): coverage is nearly as comprehensive as Cardinal Care with small cost-sharing amounts, and it remains the lowest-cost option for this income band. Virginia's Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP is the path for income above 205% FPL or for those who strongly prefer to keep an existing private network of providers. Marketplace Silver plans with Premium Tax Credits (income 100% to 400% FPL) can run $50 to $300 per month after credits, but out-of-pocket costs for prenatal and delivery care under a Marketplace plan can reach the 2026 ACA maximum out-of-pocket limit of $10,600 for an individual versus $0 under Cardinal Care. COBRA is almost never the right choice for pregnant Virginians who qualify for Medicaid or FAMIS MOMS, since COBRA charges 102% of the full premium (often $500 to $2,000 per month) for the same prenatal benefits Virginia provides free or at very low cost.
paragraphs.es: Tres programas sirven a las virginianas embarazadas en 2026 y la decision fluye logicamente desde el ingreso. Cardinal Care Medicaid es la primera verificacion: si el ingreso del hogar (contando el bebe esperado) es igual o inferior al 148% FPL ($32,028 para un hogar de 2 personas en 2026), Cardinal Care es gratuito, cubre todo y debe ser la eleccion automatica. FAMIS MOMS es el programa puente para ingresos entre 148% y 205% FPL ($32,028 a $44,362 para un hogar de 2 personas): la cobertura es casi tan completa como Cardinal Care con pequeños costos compartidos. El SEP de embarazo del Mercado de Seguros de Virginia es el camino para ingresos superiores al 205% FPL o para quienes prefieren mantener una red privada existente de proveedores. COBRA casi nunca es la eleccion correcta para las virginianas embarazadas que califican para Medicaid o FAMIS MOMS.

en.question: What is the income limit for pregnancy Medicaid in Virginia in 2026?
en.answer: Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid for pregnant women covers income up to 148% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level. A pregnant woman counts as two people (she plus the expected baby), so the 2026 income limit is $32,028 per year for a household of two, $40,434 for a household of three, and $48,840 for a household of four. FAMIS MOMS (Virginia CHIP for pregnant women) extends coverage to 205% FPL: $44,362 for a 2-person household and $56,006 for a 3-person household. Both programs accept applications year-round through commonhelp.virginia.gov or coverva.dmas.virginia.gov.

en.question: How do I apply for pregnancy Medicaid in Virginia in 2026?
en.answer: Apply online at commonhelp.virginia.gov, through the CoverVA portal at coverva.dmas.virginia.gov, or by calling Virginia DMAS at 1-855-242-8282. You can also apply in person at your local Virginia Department of Social Services office. Gather proof of identity (Virginia ID or passport), proof of Virginia residency (utility bill or lease), proof of pregnancy (healthcare provider's note or prenatal records), and documentation of all income sources for everyone in your household. Most applications are processed within 45 days. Ask your prenatal provider about presumptive eligibility to start coverage immediately during the review period.

en.question: What is the Virginia pregnancy SEP for the Marketplace in 2026?
en.answer: Virginia created a new pregnancy-specific Special Enrollment Period for its state-based Insurance Marketplace effective January 31, 2026. Before this law, becoming pregnant was not a qualifying life event under federal ACA rules. The new Virginia pregnancy SEP lets any qualifying pregnant person who is not already enrolled in a Marketplace plan enroll in a private plan at any point during pregnancy. Once you start the enrollment process at marketplace.virginia.gov, you have 60 days to select and finalize a plan. The SEP is only available to new Marketplace enrollees, not to those already enrolled who want to switch plans.

en.question: How long does pregnancy Medicaid coverage last in Virginia?
en.answer: Virginia Medicaid for pregnant women covers prenatal care, labor and delivery, and then continues for 12 full months after the end of pregnancy. This 12-month postpartum extension became permanent in Virginia under the American Rescue Plan Act provisions and cannot be terminated due to income changes during that postpartum year. FAMIS MOMS follows the same 12-month postpartum rule. After the postpartum year ends, standard Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid is available for adults at up to 138% FPL if your income qualifies. If not, you may transition to a Marketplace plan using a qualifying life event SEP.

en.question: What happens to my baby's health insurance after birth in Virginia?
en.answer: Babies born to Cardinal Care Medicaid-enrolled mothers are automatically enrolled in Virginia Medicaid at birth under the deemed newborn rule, with coverage retroactive to the date of birth. The hospital typically handles this enrollment. The baby remains enrolled for 12 months of continuous coverage regardless of income changes. If the mother is on FAMIS MOMS rather than Cardinal Care, the newborn may enroll in FAMIS (Virginia CHIP for children up to 205% FPL) or Cardinal Care for children (up to 148% FPL). If the mother is on a Marketplace or COBRA plan at delivery, the birth triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period to add the newborn to coverage.

en.question: Is COBRA worth it for pregnant women in Virginia?
en.answer: Almost never, if you qualify for Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid or FAMIS MOMS. COBRA charges 102% of the full employer premium, typically $500 to $2,000 per month for individual coverage. Cardinal Care provides the same comprehensive prenatal and delivery coverage at zero cost for income up to 148% FPL, and FAMIS MOMS provides near-zero-cost coverage to 205% FPL. The only scenario where COBRA might make sense is if your income is well above 205% FPL and you need to maintain coverage with a specific high-risk obstetric specialist who is not in the Virginia Marketplace network. Even then, compare the COBRA monthly cost against a Marketplace Silver plan with Premium Tax Credits before deciding.

en.question: Does Cardinal Care Medicaid cover prenatal care even if my pregnancy started before I enrolled?
en.answer: Yes. Virginia Cardinal Care and FAMIS MOMS cover prenatal care from the application date or presumptive eligibility determination date, regardless of when the pregnancy began. Additionally, Virginia Medicaid may provide retroactive coverage for up to 3 months prior to the application month in some cases, which means prenatal care received before you applied may be covered retroactively. Ask your DMAS case worker at 1-855-242-8282 about retroactive eligibility when you apply. The Virginia Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP similarly covers maternity care and childbirth as essential health benefits even if the pregnancy began before the Marketplace enrollment start date.

en.question: What state-specific Virginia programs exist beyond standard Medicaid for pregnant women?
en.answer: Virginia offers several programs that go beyond standard federal Medicaid. FAMIS MOMS extends coverage to 205% FPL for pregnant women who exceed the 148% Cardinal Care threshold. Presumptive eligibility lets qualified healthcare providers authorize immediate prenatal coverage before a formal Medicaid determination. The 12-month postpartum extension is now permanent in Virginia, going further than the 60-day federal floor. Virginia's own state-based Insurance Marketplace at marketplace.virginia.gov (separate from healthcare.gov) hosts the new pregnancy-specific SEP effective January 31, 2026, a benefit not federally required and not available in all states. Virginia FAMIS covers children up to 205% FPL with year-round enrollment and 12-month continuous coverage protection.

es.question: Cual es el limite de ingresos para Medicaid de embarazo en Virginia en 2026?
es.answer: Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid para mujeres embarazadas cubre ingresos hasta el 148% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026. Una mujer embarazada cuenta como dos personas (ella mas el bebe esperado), por lo que el limite de ingresos de 2026 es $32,028 por ano para un hogar de dos personas, $40,434 para un hogar de tres personas y $48,840 para un hogar de cuatro personas. FAMIS MOMS (CHIP de Virginia para mujeres embarazadas) extiende la cobertura al 205% FPL: $44,362 para un hogar de 2 personas y $56,006 para un hogar de 3 personas. Ambos programas aceptan solicitudes todo el ano a traves de commonhelp.virginia.gov o coverva.dmas.virginia.gov.

es.question: Como solicito Medicaid de embarazo en Virginia en 2026?
es.answer: Solicite en linea en commonhelp.virginia.gov, a traves del portal CoverVA en coverva.dmas.virginia.gov, o llamando a Virginia DMAS al 1-855-242-8282. Tambien puede solicitar en persona en su oficina local del Departamento de Servicios Sociales de Virginia. Reuna prueba de identidad, prueba de residencia en Virginia, prueba de embarazo y documentacion de todas las fuentes de ingresos de todos en su hogar. La mayoria de las solicitudes se procesan en 45 dias. Pregunte a su proveedor prenatal sobre la elegibilidad presuntiva para comenzar la cobertura de inmediato durante el periodo de revision.

es.question: Que es el SEP de embarazo de Virginia para el Mercado en 2026?
es.answer: Virginia creo un nuevo Periodo de Inscripcion Especial especifico para el embarazo para su Mercado de Seguros estatal efectivo el 31 de enero de 2026. Antes de esta ley, quedar embarazada no era un evento calificador de vida bajo las reglas federales de la ACA. El nuevo SEP de embarazo de Virginia permite a cualquier persona embarazada calificada que no este inscrita en un plan del Mercado inscribirse en un plan privado en cualquier momento durante el embarazo. Una vez que inicia el proceso de inscripcion en marketplace.virginia.gov, tiene 60 dias para seleccionar y finalizar un plan. El SEP solo esta disponible para nuevos inscriptos del Mercado.

es.question: Cuanto dura la cobertura de Medicaid de embarazo en Virginia?
es.answer: Virginia Medicaid para mujeres embarazadas cubre la atencion prenatal, el parto y luego continua por 12 meses completos despues del fin del embarazo. Esta extension postparto de 12 meses se volvio permanente en Virginia y no puede terminarse debido a cambios de ingresos durante ese ano postparto. FAMIS MOMS sigue la misma regla postparto de 12 meses. Despues de que termina el ano postparto, el Cardinal Care Medicaid estandar de Virginia esta disponible para adultos hasta 138% FPL si su ingreso califica.

es.question: Que pasa con el seguro medico de mi bebe despues del nacimiento en Virginia?
es.answer: Los bebes nacidos de madres inscritas en Cardinal Care Medicaid se inscriben automaticamente en Medicaid de Virginia al nacer bajo la regla del recien nacido calificado, con cobertura retroactiva a la fecha de nacimiento. El hospital generalmente se encarga de esta inscripcion. El bebe permanece inscrito durante 12 meses de cobertura continua independientemente de los cambios de ingreso. Si la madre esta en FAMIS MOMS, el recien nacido puede inscribirse en FAMIS (CHIP de Virginia para ninos hasta 205% FPL) o Cardinal Care para ninos (hasta 148% FPL).

es.question: Vale la pena COBRA para mujeres embarazadas en Virginia?
es.answer: Casi nunca, si califica para Virginia Cardinal Care Medicaid o FAMIS MOMS. COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima completa del empleador, tipicamente $500 a $2,000 por mes para cobertura individual. Cardinal Care proporciona la misma cobertura prenatal y de parto a cero costo para ingresos hasta 148% FPL, y FAMIS MOMS proporciona cobertura a costo casi nulo hasta 205% FPL. El unico escenario donde COBRA podria tener sentido es si su ingreso esta muy por encima del 205% FPL y necesita mantener cobertura con un especialista obstetrico especifico que no esta en la red del Mercado de Virginia.

es.question: Cardinal Care Medicaid cubre la atencion prenatal aunque mi embarazo haya comenzado antes de inscribirme?
es.answer: Si. Virginia Cardinal Care y FAMIS MOMS cubren la atencion prenatal desde la fecha de solicitud o la fecha de determinacion de elegibilidad presuntiva, independientemente de cuando comenzo el embarazo. Ademas, Medicaid de Virginia puede proporcionar cobertura retroactiva por hasta 3 meses antes del mes de solicitud en algunos casos. Pregunte a su trabajador de caso de DMAS al 1-855-242-8282 sobre la elegibilidad retroactiva cuando solicite. El SEP de embarazo del Mercado de Seguros de Virginia tambien cubre la maternidad y el parto como beneficios esenciales de salud aunque el embarazo haya comenzado antes de la fecha de inicio de inscripcion.

es.question: Que programas especificos de Virginia existen mas alla del Medicaid estandar para mujeres embarazadas?
es.answer: Virginia ofrece varios programas que van mas alla del Medicaid federal estandar. FAMIS MOMS extiende la cobertura al 205% FPL. La elegibilidad presuntiva permite que proveedores calificados autoricen cobertura prenatal inmediata antes de una determinacion formal de Medicaid. La extension postparto de 12 meses es ahora permanente en Virginia. El Mercado de Seguros estatal de Virginia en marketplace.virginia.gov alberga el nuevo SEP especifico para el embarazo efectivo el 31 de enero de 2026. Virginia FAMIS cubre ninos hasta 205% FPL con inscripcion todo el ano y proteccion de cobertura continua de 12 meses.

en: Incorrect household size: not counting the expected baby as a household member, which lowers the stated income threshold and can incorrectly appear to disqualify applicants who actually qualify
Using prior-year tax income instead of projected current 2026 income: Virginia Medicaid uses MAGI based on projected annual income, not last year's tax return
Missing or outdated proof of pregnancy: applications without a current provider note or prenatal record confirming pregnancy are placed on hold

Applying through healthcare.gov instead of Virginia's state portal: Virginia residents must use commonhelp.virginia.gov or coverva.dmas.virginia.gov for Medicaid, and marketplace.virginia.gov for Marketplace plans
Overstating income by including non-MAGI items: MAGI for Medicaid excludes child support received, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and most veterans benefits
es: Tamano del hogar incorrecto: no contar al bebe esperado como miembro del hogar, lo que reduce el umbral de ingreso declarado y puede hacer que los solicitantes que realmente califican parezcan no calificar

Usar el ingreso fiscal del ano anterior en lugar del ingreso proyectado actual para 2026: Medicaid de Virginia usa MAGI basado en el ingreso anual proyectado, no en la declaracion de impuestos del ano pasado
Prueba de embarazo faltante o desactualizada: las solicitudes sin una nota actual del proveedor o un registro prenatal que confirme el embarazo se ponen en espera

Solicitar a traves de healthcare.gov en lugar del portal estatal de Virginia: los residentes de Virginia deben usar commonhelp.virginia.gov o coverva.dmas.virginia.gov para Medicaid, y marketplace.virginia.gov para planes del Mercado

Sobreestimar los ingresos incluyendo elementos que no son MAGI: el MAGI para Medicaid excluye la manutencion de hijos recibida, el Ingreso de Seguridad Suplementario (SSI) y la mayoria de los beneficios de veteranos

stateRules.rule: Cardinal Care Medicaid for pregnant women covers income up to 148% FPL (2026). FAMIS MOMS (CHIP for pregnant women) covers up to 205% FPL. Effective January 31, 2026, Virginia created a pregnancy-specific SEP for its state-based Insurance Marketplace at marketplace.virginia.gov, not healthcare.gov. Postpartum coverage extends 12 months after delivery under ARP permanent extension. Presumptive eligibility allows same-day prenatal care authorization by qualified providers. Babies born to Medicaid mothers are auto-enrolled (deemed newborn rule).

heading.es: Cardinal Care vs FAMIS MOMS vs Mercado vs COBRA: Que Cobertura Debe Elegir en Virginia?

body.en: Three public programs and one private option serve pregnant Virginians in 2026, and income drives the decision tree. Cardinal Care Medicaid is the clear first choice at 148% FPL or below ($32,028 annual for a 2-person household in 2026), providing zero-cost prenatal care, labor and delivery, and a full 12 months of postpartum coverage. FAMIS MOMS fills the gap from 148% to 205% FPL ($32,028 to $44,362 for a 2-person household): similar comprehensive benefits with modest cost-sharing, still far cheaper than any private plan. Virginia's Insurance Marketplace pregnancy SEP, new effective January 31, 2026 at marketplace.virginia.gov, opens private plan access for income above 205% FPL or for those preferring to keep an existing provider network. Marketplace Silver plans run $50 to $300 per month after Premium Tax Credits for income between 100% and 400% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level, but out-of-pocket costs at delivery can reach the 2026 ACA maximum out-of-pocket limit of $10,600 for an individual. COBRA continuation from a former employer averages $500 to $2,000 per month for the same prenatal coverage Virginia provides free or at very low cost under Cardinal Care and FAMIS MOMS. The decision matrix for 2026: check Cardinal Care first (free, no deadline, apply at coverva.dmas.virginia.gov); check FAMIS MOMS second (very low cost, same application portal); use the Virginia Marketplace pregnancy SEP third (private network option, 60-day completion window once started); consider COBRA only as a last resort if your specialist network is critical and not available in any Marketplace plan.
body.es: Tres programas publicos y una opcion privada sirven a las virginianas embarazadas en 2026, y el ingreso impulsa el arbol de decision. Cardinal Care Medicaid es la primera eleccion clara al 148% FPL o menos ($32,028 anuales para un hogar de 2 personas en 2026), proporcionando atencion prenatal de costo cero, parto y 12 meses completos de cobertura postparto. FAMIS MOMS llena la brecha del 148% al 205% FPL ($32,028 a $44,362 para un hogar de 2 personas): beneficios integrales similares con costos compartidos modestos, aun mucho mas baratos que cualquier plan privado. El SEP de embarazo del Mercado de Seguros de Virginia, nuevo efectivo el 31 de enero de 2026 en marketplace.virginia.gov, abre el acceso a planes privados para ingresos superiores al 205% FPL o para quienes prefieren mantener una red de proveedores existente. Los planes Silver del Mercado cuestan $50 a $300 por mes despues de Creditos Fiscales de Prima. COBRA continua de un empleador anterior promedia $500 a $2,000 por mes por la misma cobertura prenatal que Virginia proporciona gratis o a costo muy bajo bajo Cardinal Care y FAMIS MOMS.
